Hi Jane �14 thanks for the screenshot, that helps. This is a known Google Calendar behavior when the organizer's calendar defaults are set to a different zone or the event was created via a third-party tool that omits timezone metadata. Steps I took and recommended fixes below �14 I also attached a corrected ICS that explicitly sets the timezone to Europe/London for start/end.

What I did (and what to ask attendees to do if they still see issues):
1) Re-created the event directly in Google Calendar and explicitly clicked the time zone selector -> set Start/End to Europe/London (BST).
2) Added the meeting as a Google Meet event (not a forwarded static invite) so Google surfaces the timezone in the event header.
3) Sent a separate invite variant for APAC (I included an APAC-friendly time option) so those attendees get a dedicated event in their local zone instead of relying on a single floating invite.
4) If someone already forwarded the original invite, ask them to delete the forwarded copy and accept the new event (forwarded copies keep the original metadata).

Attached: 20260407-redwood-demo-fixed.ics

If people still see wrong times, two quick troubleshooting tips for attendees: open the event details -> click the three-dot menu -> "Event details" and check the time zone; or open the event in the web UI (not mobile) and confirm the start/end show the Europe/London timezone string.

I'll leave the corrected event live and send a follow-up with a short agenda. Camila / Dylan �14 FYI in case we want to lock the APAC variant now.
